subject: How to define fractions in parameter contraints?

messages.author: 3f3060000990daa6
messages.subject: How to define fractions in parameter contraints?
parts:
Hi all,

I want to test a model where the constraint on one parameters is defined by the fraction of two other parameters.

Here's a simple example:

z ~ b1*x + b2*y + b3*xy
b1== (b2/b3)

This obviously introduces a singularity when b3 == 0. But adding another constraint tp prevent this singularity (e.g. b3 > 1) did not help.

Here's a reproducible snippet:

set.seed(0xBEEF)
n <- 300
err <- 2
x <- rnorm(n, 0, 5)
y <- rnorm(n, 0, 5)
df <- data.frame(x, y)
df <- within(df, {
    z <- 0.5*x + 0.2*y + 0.3*xy + rnorm(n, 0, err)
    xy <- x*y
})


model <-  paste("z ~ b1*x + b2*y + b3*xy",
    "b3 > 1",
    "b1 == (b2/b3)",
    sep="\n")
fit <-  sem(model, data=df, fixed.x=FALSE, meanstructure=TRUE)


Q1: Is there a way to specify the constraint b3 != 0? (That syntax does not work)
Q2: Is there any way at all to define these fractional constraints? (I am not sure why the example above does not work).

Thanks,
Felix

On 10/17/2012 08:52 AM, Felix Sch�nbrodt wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> I want to test a model where the constraint on one parameters is defined
> by the fraction of two other parameters.
>
> Here's a simple example:
>
> z ~ b1*x + b2*y + b3*xy
> b1== (b2/b3)
>
> This obviously introduces a singularity when b3 == 0. But adding another
> constraint tp prevent this singularity (e.g. b3 > 1) did not help.

It is starting value issue. By default, all starting values for the
regression coefficients are zero. This usually works well, but not of
course if your case.

> Q1: Is there a way to specify the constraint b3 != 0? (That syntax does
> not work)
No. This is not defined (and I see no easy way to implement this).
> Q2: Is there any way at all to define these fractional constraints? (I

> am not sure why the example above does not work).*

Provide starting values that obey your constraints (at the very least:
b1 > 0):

This seems to work:

model <- paste("z ~ b1*x + b2*y + b3*xy + start(1.2)*xy",

Estimate Std.err Z-value P(>|z|)
Regressions:
z ~
x (b1) 0.391 0.125 3.116 0.002
y (b2) 0.391 0.125 3.116 0.002
xy (b3) 1.000 NA


Yves.

Thanks Yves! That helped me a lot.
As a preliminary solution, I run two models, one with contraint b1 < 0, and one with b1 > 0.

If anybody finds a solution for implementing a b1 != 0 constraint: I would welcome this ;-)

Cheers,
Felix
